title: POC scoping - Data handling & retention
next_steps: Alex to share SOC 2 + ISO docs and KMS integration guide by 2025-06-20
Priya to provide benchmark template and sample workload config by 2025-06-22
Customer to provide 3 redacted example prompts and expected success criteria by 2025-06-24
Schedule 1-hour pilot kickoff (benchmarks) with infra team week of 2025-06-30
action_items: Alex - Send security pack (SOC2/ISO, audit logs, KMS) - due 2025-06-20
Priya - Share perf benchmark spreadsheet + recommended dataset slice - due 2025-06-22
Ben - Confirm VPC peering constraints and egress rules - due 2025-06-23
Sara/Ryan - Provide sample prompts and PII policy for redaction tests - due 2025-06-24
summary: POC scoping focused on data handling for a 4-week pilot: redaction and retention requirements, logging controls, prompt storage concerns, success criteria and throughput/latency targets. Agreed next steps include sharing security docs, bench template, and scheduling benchmark run.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the POC scope around data handling. we're aiming for, like, a 3-4 week pilot, yes.
[00:08] Sara Cole: Yep, Sara here. We'll focus on customer support automation for now, coupled with some document Q&A. Major concern is PII leakage and auditability.
[00:17] Ben Li: Ben here. Security architect. We'll need to validate retention settings, KMS integration, and how prompts are stored. Also need to know what logs Redwood keeps by default.
[00:26] Priya Singh: Priya from Redwood, SE. We'll cover default logging, redaction hooks, and options: hosted vs dedicated vs private. Also go through benchmarks for latency and throughput.
[00:36] Ryan Park: Ryan here. From ML. We care about latency around 200ms for short completions and concurrency ~100 qps for burst. We'll size workload as we discuss.
[00:47] Alex Martinez: Cool. Agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, and then deep dive on data handling: PII, logging, retention, prompt storage.
[00:58] Priya Singh: For the POC success criteria, can we write them down? Typical ones we see: 1) latency SLOs met X% of the time, 2) acceptable output quality compared to baseline, 3) demonstrable redaction/retention controls, 4) integration feasibility with your infra.
[01:15] Sara Cole: Quality baseline is important. We'll provide a small eval set. For data handling we need to ensure that raw prompts containing PII are either not stored or are redacted.
[01:24] Ben Li: On retention: we want a max of 30 days for prompt storage in the POC, encrypted at rest, and ability to purge on demand. Also need audit logs for access to prompts.
[01:33] Priya Singh: Right, Redwood supports retention settings per-tenant for Dedicated and private deployments; hosted can do configurable retention with options for zero-retention where we don't store prompts beyond request processing. But note zero-retention affects debugging and some observability features.
[01:50] Alex Martinez: Alex interjects: also note for hosted we offer a 'no-persist' mode for POCs; it's an opt-in setting that disables prompt retention, and we'll show how logs can be scrubbed.
[02:02] Ryan Park: If we do no-persist, how do we run bench results that need example inputs? We need a sanitized sample.
[02:10] Priya Singh: You'd provide sanitized samples. For benchmarking, we run your workload in a sandbox with telemetry that captures token counts, latency percentiles, and error rates. The telemetry can be configured to exclude prompt text and only record meta metrics.
[02:24] Sara Cole: Good. What about KMS? We use customer-managed keys for encryption - must integrate with our cloud KMS.
[02:31] Priya Singh: We support KMS/HSM integration in Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via a limited KMS integration - we'll need to verify with your provider. I'll include integration docs.
[02:45] Ben Li: Audit logs - who can see the prompts? We need role-based access control and record of any manual access to raw text.
[02:52] Alex Martinez: Redwood Console exposes RBAC for console access and API keys; access to raw transcript storage is gated. For the POC we'll limit access to the SE+your team and log any access. We'll provide an export of audit events for the test window.
[03:06] Priya Singh: On redaction, we have two patterns: client-side redaction where the customer strips or masks PII before sending, and server-side redaction hooks where Redwood can run a redaction pipeline (regex/ML) before any persistence. Server-side redaction is offered as an option but increases processing latency slightly.
[03:26] Sara Cole: We prefer server-side redaction for safety but we'll want to test accuracy. What are typical false positives/negatives?
[03:32] Priya Singh: It depends; regex-based is high precision for structured identifiers (SSNs, emails), ML-based entity detection can catch contextual PII but needs tuning. For the POC we'll run both and produce a redaction report. Expect an initial 2-5% miss rate for unstructured PII in generic models, but we can tune on your sample set.
[03:54] Ryan Park: Benchmarks - let's talk numbers. We're aiming for p50 ~120ms, p95 < 350ms for short responses, concurrency 80 sustained and 150 burst. Cost is also a concern - we want guidance on model variant and quantization.
[04:12] Priya Singh: For that workload, Dedicated with a 1-2 GPU pool using an optimized quantized variant should meet those SLOs. For hosted, we can run a canary on a higher perf instance to validate latency, then propose Dedicated sizing. We'll provide a benchmark template.
[04:28] Alex Martinez: Success criteria recap: latency thresholds met on your sample, redaction accuracy >= 98% for structured PII and acceptable improvements for unstructured, retention/purge verified, and secure KMS integration.
[04:42] Ben Li: For purge verification, we want a process: issue purge request via API, get confirmation and proof that data is removed. Any drift in logs? We need a tamper-evident audit.
[04:53] Priya Singh: We can provide purge receipts and timestamped audit events. For tamper evidence, we can export signed logs during the POC window. For production we recommend isolating storage and using customer-managed keys.
[05:07] Sara Cole: How are prompts stored in the database? Are they hashed? Encrypted?
[05:12] Priya Singh: Prompts at rest are encrypted; in Dedicated/Private you can bring KMS. Hashing isn't used for retrieval, since we need the raw prompt for debugging unless disabled. With no-persist mode we avoid storage entirely.
[05:26] Ryan Park: Is there a way to store embeddings only and throw away prompts? We want to retain semantic index without raw text.
[05:33] Priya Singh: Yes, you can persist embeddings and metadata only. We have support for configurable persistence layers so prompts can be dropped while embeddings and metadata are kept. We'll demo that pattern.
[05:45] Alex Martinez: Let's circle back to benchmarking timeline. Proposed schedule: week 0: share docs and sample set, week 1: Redwood runs internal bench and shares results, week 2: joint benchmark with your infra (VPC/dedicated), week 3: iterate on redaction and tuning, week 4: handoff + runbook. Does that work?
[06:01] Sara Cole: That's reasonable. We have a compliance review at the end of month, so finishing by July 18 would be ideal.
[06:09] Ben Li: On network setup, we may require VPC peering or private link. Are there constraints?
[06:15] Priya Singh: We support VPC peering for Dedicated and Private; hosted can use PrivateLink for selective customers. For the POC we can run over secure egress with IP allowlist if needed. I'll include the network checklist.
[06:28] Ryan Park: For perf tests, will you run both streaming and non-streaming paths? Our UX uses short streaming completions for chat.
[06:34] Priya Singh: Yes, we'll test both streaming and chunked non-stream. Streaming has slightly different latency characteristics; we'll capture token throughput and end-to-end time.
[06:44] Alex Martinez: Regarding artifacts we'll share: SOC2 + ISO summary, KMS guide, redaction whitepaper, benchmark template, and a sample benchmark runbook. Link to security pack: https://redwood.example/security-pack (placeholder).
[06:56] Sara Cole: Perfect. For success criteria, we'll also define acceptance on quality: for our 100-example eval, >= 90% intent match and no PII leakage incidents.
[07:05] Priya Singh: We'll set up an evaluation harness for that. We'll also run regression checks against your eval.
[07:12] Ben Li: One more question: How long do logs live by default in hosted?
[07:16] Alex Martinez: Default retention is 90 days for hosted telemetry; prompt retention is configurable and defaults to 30 days, but we can set it to 0 for the POC. Dedicated/Private defaults are customer-controlled.
[07:29] Sara Cole: Ok. For legal we may need DPA addendum - is that part of the POC?
[07:34] Alex Martinez: We can provide a standard DPA; legal review might be parallel to the POC but we'll share the template now.
[07:42] Ryan Park: Anything else on prompt storage? We want to ensure prompt metadata (request id, timestamp, hashed user id) persists for debugging without the raw text.
[07:50] Priya Singh: That's supported - store metadata and hashed identifiers while redacting raw text. We'll outline the exact fields we'll keep by default.
[07:59] Ben Li: Regarding redaction performance penalty, do you have numbers?
[08:03] Priya Singh: Regex redaction is negligible (ms); ML redaction adds ~20-50ms depending on model. We'll measure in the bench.
[08:12] Sara Cole: For the bench, can you simulate our traffic shape? It's variable with diurnal spikes up to 150 qps.
[08:19] Priya Singh: Yes, include qps curve and payload size distribution in the template. We'll simulate with our load harness.
[08:27] Alex Martinez: Alright, recap of next steps - Alex will send security pack and DPA; Priya will send bench template and run a preliminary internal baseline; Acme provides sample prompts and PII policy. We'll set the kickoff for week of June 30.
[08:42] Ryan Park: Sounds good.
[08:44] Sara Cole: Thanks, everyone.
[08:46] Alex Martinez: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite and links.
[08:50] [meeting ends]
